driven_axle.conclusion: front-wheel drive: front wheels over-speed under throttle; the REAR (non-driven) axle mean is the slip-free speed reference

unit_decision.why_not: H_kmh and H_rads differ by a constant factor only; every kinematic relation (speed, left/right turn differential, gear ratios) scales identically, so the label cannot be proven from this data
evidence: rear-axle mean equals VBOX speed in km/h to a factor 1.00019: the expected result for a calibrated km/h signal
under rad/s the rear rolling radius would have to be 0.27772 m, i.e. exactly 1/3.6 m to within the calibration spread -- a coincidence
the channel tracks CAN 'Indicated Vehicle Speed (km/hr)' to ~0.1 %
unit_decision.ground_truth_consequence: none: the empirical factor above converts the channel to m/s regardless of the label

gnss_latency.rule: accepted if corr >= 0.9 and within [0.0, 10.0] s

phone_gps_speed_unit.question: unit of the phone 'GPS SPEED (Kmh)' column
phone_gps_speed_unit.method: median(logged phone speed / VBOX Doppler speed [m/s]) at the fix epoch, VBOX speed > 5 m/s, sessions with a measured GNSS latency
phone_gps_speed_unit.conclusion: m/s -- the 'Kmh' header is wrong (Android Location.getSpeed returns m/s). Phases 0-2 divided the value by 3.6; fixed in Phase 3.

split.unit: drive (connected sessions: same driver and same route group or gap < 600 s)
